current_status.stage: Approved and commercialized across Europe and select Asian/African markets since the 1980s under a long-running Debiopharm (owner/developer)–Ipsen (commercialization) partnership extended through 2034. Indicated for prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, central precocious puberty, and early-stage hormone-responsive breast cancer.
current_status.data_point: FY2025: Decapeptyl cited by Ipsen among products facing increased European and Chinese competition/pricing pressure, tempering growth versus the rest of Ipsen's non-Somatuline portfolio (which grew 14.2% overall)

finding_history.summary: Debiopharm and Ipsen extended their Decapeptyl (triptorelin pamoate) partnership — originally established in the 1980s — for a further 15 years through 2034, covering development, manufacturing, and distribution across Europe and select Asian and African markets, and committing to co-develop new formulations and explore additional indications. Decapeptyl generated €372.6M in sales in 2018 (+8.1% y/y) at the time of the announcement.

Ipsen's FY2025 results announcement (2026-02-12) reported overall FY2025 sales growth of 10.9% (constant exchange rates), with all products excluding Somatuline growing 14.2% in aggregate; Decapeptyl was not broken out with specific figures in the release itself. Separately, third-party financial coverage of Ipsen's 2025 quarterly disclosures characterized Decapeptyl as facing increased competition and pricing pressure in Europe and China, with more modest growth (e.g. +2.2% in Q3 2025) than the broader portfolio.
